report.releaseDate: 16 Oct 2026 (ADG Event Wagering & Fantasy Sports Revenue Reports – August 2026, unaudited)
report.verdict: August 2026 was Arizona's softest month of the year: handle $582.8m (−4.6% YoY, −2.8% MoM), gross hold back to ~8.7% from an unusually book-friendly 10.1% a year earlier, and state privilege fees down 12% to ~$3.6m — a reminder that a 10%-of-adjusted-receipts, promo-deductible regime yields the state only ~0.6% of handle. Structurally nothing moved: a 99.7% mobile market, FanDuel/DraftKings holding 60% of handle (top four 82%), licence access gated through tribes or pro-sports franchises, and a governor who has already put a 45% rate for scale operators on the table.
summary: **Handle fell to a 2026 low.** Arizonans wagered $582.8m on sports and events in August 2026 per the Arizona Department of Gaming (ADG), −4.6% YoY against $610.7m in August 2025 and −2.8% MoM against $599.5m in July. It is the second YoY decline in four months (May −4.3%) after June (+22.3%) and July (+29.3%) were flattered — on our reading — by the FIFA World Cup window; ADG itself offers no attribution.

**Mobile is the market.** $581.2m (99.7%) was staked via mobile apps and $1.6m (0.3%) at retail books and Limited Event Wagering Operator (LEWO) sites; retail handle fell ~11% YoY. AGA puts mobile at 99.5% of CY2025 statewide sportsbook revenue ($838.7m) with retail revenue of just $2.7m.

**Hold normalised and revenue fell faster than handle.** Operators paid out ~$532m, implying gross win of ~$50.8m (8.7% of handle) versus ~$61.4m (10.1%) in August 2025 — a −17% YoY swing in gross revenue on −4.6% handle (derived from ADG-reported payouts; the ADG line items are labelled unaudited and self-reported).

**Promo deductions remain the biggest wedge between GGR and the tax base.** Privilege fees of ~$3.6m at the 10% mobile rate imply ~$36m of taxable adjusted gross event wagering receipts (AGEWR), so roughly $13m of free bets/promotional credits were deducted (~27% of pre-promo AGEWR, ~2.3% of handle) — down from $18.4m (31%) in August 2025 and $21.7m (41%) in June 2026.

**The state's yield is thin by design.** FY2026 (Jul-25–Jun-26): handle $9,077.5m, AGEWR subject to privilege fees $579.2m (6.4% of handle), event-wagering privilege fees $57.76m (9.97% of the taxable base), total EWFS privilege and licensing fees $61.08m (ADG FY2026 Annual Report). Cumulative since the 9 Sep 2021 launch: $37.1bn handle, $202.5m fees — 0.55% of handle.

**FY2027 has started with volume up but fees down.** Jul–Aug 2026 handle of $1,182.3m is ~+10% on the same months of FY2026 (derived), yet privilege fees of $11.8m ($11.5m event wagering + $238,714 fantasy) sit below the ~$10m+ run-rate implied by last year's hold; June 2026 showed the extreme case — handle +22% YoY, taxable AGEWR down to $30.7m from $50.5m, fees −39%.

**A duopoly with a credible #3.** August handle: FanDuel $186.4m (32.0%), DraftKings $163.4m (28.0%), Fanatics $71.0m (12.2%), BetMGM ~$55m (9.4%), bet365 ~$43m (7.4%), Caesars ~$31m (5.3%), Hard Rock ~$11m (1.9%), theScore Bet ~$8m (1.4%); all others (Desert Diamond, BetRivers, Bally Bet, Golden Nugget, retail/LEWO) ~$14m (2.4%). Top-two 60%, top-four 82%. FanDuel regained the handle lead it lost to DraftKings in June ($197m vs $195m) and consistently leads on revenue (Jan–Feb 2026 gross: FanDuel $50.8m vs DraftKings $45.8m on 11%+ holds).

**Licensing is capped and partner-gated.** HB 2772 (signed 15 Apr 2021; A.R.S. §5-1301 et seq.) allows a maximum of 20 event wagering operator licences — 10 for tribes that signed the 2021 Amended & Restated Compact and 10 for professional sports franchises/facilities (incl. the PGA Tour tournament host, the NASCAR promoter and a Maricopa County horse-racing permittee) — each with one mobile platform plus retail within five blocks of the venue, plus up to 10 retail-only LEWO licences for racetracks/OTBs. ADG lists 15 event wagering licensees, two of which have ceased and one has not launched (Fox10, Sep-26); a trade tracker counted 18 of 20 slots issued in March 2026 — the gap reflects surrendered allocations.

**New supply is trickling in.** ADG re-opened applications for available licences in May 2026 and on 3 Aug 2026 allocated an operator licence to Circa Sports Arizona LLC as designee of the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe, with launch potentially in Q1 2027. Sporttrade (Quechan Tribe designee, launched 26 Sep 2024) exited after just $20.4m cumulative handle and $290,581 gross revenue through March 2026; PENN's ESPN Bet was replaced by theScore Bet.

**Tax regime: 10% mobile / 8% retail on AGEWR, statutory cap 10%.** A.R.S. §5-1318 caps the privilege fee at 10% of AGEWR (gross receipts ex-voids, minus winnings and the 0.25% federal excise); ADG set 10% for mobile and 8% for retail. Fantasy contests pay 5% of adjusted revenue (statutory cap 10%). Fees are due by the 25th of the following month; 90% flows to the General Fund and 10% is retained by ADG in the Event Wagering Fund.

**The promo deduction is scheduled to disappear — timing unverified.** The enabling statute limits the free-bet/promo deduction to five years from 15 April 2021 on a declining cap (20% of gross receipts in years 1–2, 15% in year 3, 10% in years 4–5) and bars it thereafter; the June and August 2026 reports nonetheless still show deductions being taken, so the operative sunset date (licence-year vs statutory-year basis) is [unverified]. If applied, the taxable base would rise ~30–40% at constant GGR.

**Political risk is live.** Governor Hobbs' FY2027 executive budget (Jan 2026) proposed a 45% privilege fee for operators with ≥$75m monthly handle (ADG confirmed the handle basis) — in practice FanDuel, DraftKings, Fanatics and BetMGM — scored at $145.9m in FY2027 rising to $202.4m by FY2029. It required either a Prop 108 two-thirds supermajority in a Republican-controlled legislature or acceptance of the administration's 'fee not tax' argument; the August 2026 fee take is consistent with an unchanged 10% rate, so the hike was not in force [final budget text not reviewed]. Expect a reprise in the January 2027 budget.

**Fantasy is a legal, lightly taxed adjacency.** August 2026 in-state entry fees $8.2m, adjusted revenue $1.6m (19.5% take), privilege fees ~$78k; PrizePicks $3.5m (43%), DraftKings $2.3m (28%), FanDuel $1.0m (12%), Underdog $0.9m (11%). FY2026: entry fees $143.9m, adjusted revenue $26.6m, fees ~$1.3m.

**No online casino and no commercial casinos.** Class III casino gaming is tribal-exclusive under the 2021 compact; iGaming is not authorised and no 2026 bill advanced. Any online casino route runs through compact renegotiation with the tribes, not the legislature alone.

**Payments and player protection are standard-US, with a few Arizona specifics.** 21+; helpline 1-800-NEXT-STEP; ADG statewide self-exclusion; player funds must sit in segregated accounts with a reserve of the greater of $500,000 or player liabilities (A.A.C. R19-4); operators must intercept winnings for past-due obligations (FY2026 set-offs per ADG: Courts $393,600, child support $121,973, SNAP $6,353, AHCCCS $0); September 2026 was Responsible Gaming Education Month. Deposit-method mix is not published by ADG [n/a].

**Data quality caveat.** Since May 2025 ADG stamps every monthly report as operator self-reported and unaudited; it received 13 of 14 independent FY2025 audit reports under §5-1319 and is still reconciling over/under-payments. Monthly figures can be restated.

**Benchmarks.** Arizona ranked #5 nationally by August 2025 handle ($610.7m, behind NY, IL, NJ, OH) and #6–7 YTD; the 10% rate is the fifth-lowest among US states (vs NY 51%, IL 20–40% plus per-bet fees, NJ 19.75%). Two-year August CAGR is +8.3% (Aug-24 $496.6m), down from +23% YoY growth in 2025.

**Read-through for B2Tech.** Arizona is one of the most operator-friendly fiscal regimes in the US (effective fee ~6–7% of GGR after promo deductions), mobile-native and deep (~$9bn annual handle). But access requires a tribal or sports-franchise designee deal in a 20-slot market with few vacancies, 82% of handle sits with four brands, sub-scale entrants have failed (Sporttrade), and the governor is targeting scale operators with a 45% tier. A realistic entry outcome is a #5–#8 position at $30–55m monthly handle; the economics only work with a differentiated product and a partner revenue-share that is modelled against a 20–45% stress-case tax.

segments.name: Sports betting — mobile (the market)
segments.headline: A 2026-low $582.8m handle with hold normalising to ~8.7% and promo intensity easing; FanDuel back on top of a 60% duopoly.
narrative: ADG's August 2026 Event Wagering Revenue Report shows $582.8m staked, of which $581.2m (99.7%) came through mobile platforms and $1.6m through retail and LEWO windows. The month is the seasonal trough between MLB's regular season and the NFL's September start; the Diamondbacks' playoff push provided some support but could not offset the comparison with August 2025 ($610.7m), which had itself grown 23% YoY. The two-year August CAGR of +8.3% (from $496.6m in August 2024) is a fairer read of underlying growth than the −4.6% print, and it is well below the +18–23% rates of 2025. The May–August pattern (−4.3%, +22.3%, +29.3%, −4.6%) is in our view best explained by the June–July FIFA World Cup window pulling forward activity; ADG does not attribute drivers.

On revenue, ADG-reported payouts of ~$532m imply gross win of ~$50.8m, an 8.7% gross hold, versus ~$61.4m and 10.1% in August 2025 — a month in which books nationally ran a fourth consecutive 10%-plus hold. Stripping the 0.25% federal excise (~$1.5m) gives pre-promo AGEWR of ~$49.3m (8.5% of handle). Privilege fees of ~$3.6m at the 10% mobile rate back out a taxable base of ~$36m (6.2% of handle), implying ~$13m of free-bet and promotional-credit deductions — ~27% of pre-promo AGEWR and 2.3% of handle, compared with $18.4m (31%, 3.0%) a year earlier, $30.4m (37%, 3.1%) in the record October 2025 month and $21.7m (41%, 3.3%) in June 2026. All August 2026 revenue lines are derived from the reported payouts and fee totals and should be treated as ±$0.5m until the PDF line items are audited; the direction — lower hold and lower promo intensity — is unambiguous.

The operator table is a duopoly with a credible third. FanDuel handled $186.4m (32.0%, +4.4% YoY), DraftKings $163.4m (28.0%, −11.2% YoY from $184.0m), Fanatics $71.0m (12.2%), BetMGM ~$55m (9.4%, ~−19% YoY from $67.5m), bet365 ~$43m (7.4%), Caesars ~$31m (5.3%), Hard Rock ~$11m (1.9%) and theScore Bet ~$8m (1.4%); the remaining ~$14m (2.4%) is split among Desert Diamond (Tohono O'odham's own book), BetRivers, Bally Bet, Golden Nugget and retail/LEWO counters. The lead rotates on handle — DraftKings edged FanDuel in June 2026 ($197m vs $195m) and in August 2025 ($184.0m vs $178.5m) — but FanDuel consistently converts better: in January–February 2026 it booked $50.8m of gross revenue on 11%-plus holds against DraftKings' $45.8m (10.1% and 8.2%), while also out-spending everyone on promotions ($16.7m over the two months, $10.5m in January alone). Operator-level revenue for August 2026 is not in the sources reviewed [n/a].

Scale context matters for an entrant. Arizona was the #5 US state by handle in August 2025 and #6–7 YTD; FY2026 handle was $9.08bn and CY2025 GGR $838.7m (+18.5%, AGA) on an effective ~9.1% gross hold. Yet the state's fiscal yield is only ~0.6% of handle, and the gap between record handle and falling tax receipts (June 2026: handle +22%, fees −39%) is the political fact that drives the tax debate covered below. For B2Tech, the realistic entry outcome is the tier occupied by bet365/Caesars — $30–55m monthly handle, 5–9% share — which at an 8–9% hold and ~2–3% promo load yields ~$2–4m of monthly net revenue before partner revenue-share; Sporttrade's exit at <$1m monthly handle shows the floor below which the Arizona cost base (licence, partner, marketing, 10% fee) does not clear.

segments.name: Operator landscape & licensing regime
segments.headline: Twenty capped licences, access only via a tribal or pro-sports designee deal; 15 listed licensees, churn at the bottom, Circa the newest allocation.
narrative: The framework is HB 2772, signed as an emergency measure on 15 April 2021 and codified at A.R.S. Title 5, Chapter 10 (§5-1301 et seq.), with §5-1302(B) making ADG the primary regulator and enforcement body for event wagering and fantasy sports (EWFS); rules sit at A.A.C. R19-4. The law was negotiated alongside the 2021 Amended and Restated Tribal-State Gaming Compact, which is why the licence architecture is symmetrical: up to 10 event wagering operator licences for Arizona tribes that signed the compact, and up to 10 for owners of professional sports franchises or their designees — the statute expressly names the operator of the PGA Tour tournament venue (TPC Scottsdale), the promoter of the NASCAR national touring race (Phoenix Raceway) and a horse-racing permittee in a county above four million people (Maricopa). Each licence carries one mobile platform (typically run by a commercial designee/management services provider) and retail wagering within a five-block radius of the sports facility; a separate Limited Event Wagering Operator (LEWO) class allows up to 10 retail-only books at racetracks and OTBs. Management services provider, supplier and individual licences complete the stack. Licence and application fee amounts were not retrievable in this research [n/a]; ADG's FY2026 accounts imply ~$2.0m of licensing receipts (total EWFS fees $61.08m less $57.76m event-wagering and ~$1.33m fantasy privilege fees).

The licence stock is nearly full on paper and thinning in practice. ADG's licensee page shows 15 event wagering licensees, two marked as having ceased Arizona business and one not yet launched (as reported in September 2026), while a trade database counted 18 of the 20 slots as issued in March 2026 — the difference being allocations surrendered or lapsed. ADG's November 2025 report listed 14 mobile operators: Bally Interactive, bet365, BetMGM, Caesars (American Wagering), Desert Diamond Mobile, DraftKings/Crown Gaming, Fanatics, FanDuel, Golden Nugget Online Gaming, PENN/ESPN Bet, Plannatech, Rush Street Interactive, Seminole Hard Rock Digital and Sporttrade. Since then ESPN Bet has become theScore Bet and Sporttrade (Quechan Tribe designee, launched 26 September 2024) has withdrawn after generating only $20.4m of handle and $290,581 of gross revenue through March 2026. In May 2026 ADG announced it would accept applications for available licences, and on 3 August 2026 it allocated an operator licence to Circa Sports Arizona LLC as designee for the San Juan Southern Paiute Tribe under A.R.S. §5-1304 and A.A.C. R19-4-105/106, with launch pencilled for Q1 2027.

Concentration is extreme and stable: top-two 60% of August handle, top-four 82%, and no operator outside the top six above 2%. The practical lesson from Sporttrade and the small tribal/commercial books is that a licence buys geolocation access, not customers; the incumbents' national databases, parlay product and promo budgets (FanDuel $10.5m in one month) set the cost of entry. Circa's sharp-book, low-promo model is the only recent entrant with an obviously differentiated proposition, and its traction will be the clearest test of whether a #5–#8 position is buildable from scratch in 2027.

For B2Tech the gating item is the partner. Every commercial brand in Arizona operates as a designee of a tribe or a sports franchise; the terms of those revenue-share agreements are private [n/a], but the scarcity value of the remaining slots — and the fact that ADG allocated the latest one to a tribe-designee pairing — means the negotiation is as much about the tribe's or team's economics as the state's. Any entry plan should assume (i) a multi-year designee agreement with a revenue-share and minimum guarantee, (ii) ADG suitability review of the designee and key persons, (iii) a segregated-funds reserve of at least $500,000 from day one, and (iv) independent annual audit under §5-1319.

segments.name: Retail, fantasy sports & adjacent verticals (casino, iGaming, lottery)
segments.headline: Retail is 0.3% of handle; fantasy is a $144m-a-year entry-fee adjacency taxed at 5%; casino is tribal-exclusive and iGaming is not on the table.
narrative: Retail event wagering exists mainly as a brand asset. August 2026 retail and LEWO handle was $1.6m (0.27% of the total), down ~11% YoY from $1.8m, after $2.07m in June 2026; AGA's CY2025 data put statewide retail sportsbook revenue at $2.7m, reversing a ~$230k loss in 2024. Retail is taxed at 8% of AGEWR against 10% for mobile, which is immaterial at these volumes. The venues are the sportsbooks inside or adjacent to the professional facilities (the five-block rule) and the racetrack/OTB LEWOs regulated through ADG's Racing Division. For an entrant, a retail counter is only worth having if a sports-facility partner brings it; it does not move the economics.

Fantasy sports contests are licensed under A.R.S. §5-1201 et seq. with a privilege fee of 5% of adjusted revenue (statutory ceiling 10%, due by the 25th, with late penalties of 5% per month up to 25%). ADG's August 2026 Fantasy Sports Revenue Report shows in-state entry fees of $8.2m, adjusted revenue of $1.6m (a 19.5% take) and ~$78k of fees; PrizePicks led with $3.5m of entry fees (43%), ahead of DraftKings $2.3m (28%), FanDuel $1.0m (12%) and Underdog $0.9m (11%). FY2026 totals were $143.9m of entry fees and $26.6m of adjusted revenue (18.5% take), i.e. ~$1.3m of fees. Pick'em-style products therefore operate legally alongside sportsbooks in Arizona at half the fee rate; the House-engrossed 2026 budget reconciliation bill HB 4155 redirects fantasy and racing fee deposits into the consolidated Event Wagering Fund (§5-1318) without changing the rates.

Casino gaming is tribal-exclusive under the 2021 Amended and Restated Compact; Arizona has no commercial casinos (AGA) and the only casino-adjacent revenue data the state publishes are the tribal contribution reports (FY2026 report exists but figures were not retrieved [n/a]). Online casino is not authorised and no 2026 bill advanced; because the compact's exclusivity provisions are the binding constraint, any iGaming route would be a tribal negotiation first and legislation second. The 2021 law also authorised Arizona Lottery keno and mobile draw games; lottery figures are outside the scope of ADG reporting [n/a].

The implication for B2Tech is that the addressable regulated pool is sports betting plus fantasy. A combined sportsbook-and-pick'em stack is legal and the fantasy fee is lighter, but ADG classifies and licences them separately and the sportsbook licence is the scarce asset. There is no near-term iGaming optionality to underwrite an Arizona entry.

segments.name: Tax regime & fiscal politics
segments.headline: 10%/8% of promo-deductible AGEWR (effective ~6–7% of GGR) — the fifth-lowest US rate — with a statutory promo sunset pending and a 45% tier already proposed by the governor.
narrative: The privilege fee is levied on adjusted gross event wagering receipts: gross wagering receipts excluding voided bets, minus winnings paid and the 0.25% federal excise on handle. A.R.S. §5-1318 requires ADG to set the fee by reference to the highest revenue-share a tribe pays under the compact and caps it at 10%; ADG set 10% for mobile and 8% for retail, with operators able to elect cash or modified-accrual accounting. The statute then allows a deduction for free bets and promotional credits redeemed, capped at 20% of gross receipts in years one and two, 15% in year three and 10% in years four and five after the 15 April 2021 effective date, and bars the deduction after year five. Actual deductions have never approached the cap — 2.3–3.3% of handle in the months reviewed — but they remove 27–41% of pre-promo AGEWR from the base, cutting the effective fee to ~6–7% of GGR and ~0.6% of handle. Because the June and August 2026 reports still show deductions being taken, the operative sunset date (ADG appears to run the clock differently from a literal reading of the statute) is [unverified] and is the single most important modelling question for FY2027–28: at constant GGR, ending the deduction would lift the taxable base by roughly 30–40%.

The fiscal take is modest and volatile. FY2026 event-wagering privilege fees were $57.76m on a taxable base of $579.2m (9.97%), with total EWFS privilege and licensing fees of $61.08m; CY2025 state tax was $53.7m (+25.7%, AGA) on $838.7m of GGR; cumulative fees since launch are $202.5m on $37.1bn of handle. Monthly swings are large: October 2025 (record $967.1m handle, $83.0m GGR, $30.4m promos, $51.6m taxable) yielded $5.2m, June 2026 ($663.9m handle, +22% YoY) yielded $3.07m versus ~$5.05m a year earlier, and August 2026 yielded ~$3.6m versus $4.1m. Ninety percent of fees go to the General Fund and 10% to ADG's Event Wagering Fund for regulation and problem-gambling programmes; the House-engrossed HB 4155 folds racing and fantasy deposits into the same fund.

The political direction is unambiguous even if the first attempt failed. Governor Hobbs' FY2027 executive budget ($17.7bn, January 2026) proposed a 45% privilege fee on operators with $75m or more of monthly handle — ADG confirmed the threshold is handle, not revenue — leaving smaller books and tribal operators at 10%. On November 2025 volumes that captured FanDuel, DraftKings, Fanatics and BetMGM (three to four operators, ~75–82% of the market); the administration scored it at $145.9m in FY2027 rising to $202.4m by FY2029, as part of ~$950m of 'uncertain' revenue offsetting federal cuts. Passage required either a Prop 108 two-thirds supermajority in a Republican-controlled legislature whose appropriations chairs publicly rejected the plan, or acceptance of the administration's argument that the privilege fee is a fee rather than a tax. The August 2026 fee take is consistent with an unchanged 10% rate, so the tier was not enacted for FY2027 [the enacted budget text was not reviewed]; with the 'record handle, falling tax' narrative gaining local-media traction, we expect a reprise in the January 2027 executive budget, likely recalibrated (a lower tier rate, a promo-deduction repeal, or a per-bet fee as in Illinois).

Two federal overlays matter for modelling. The 0.25% federal excise on handle (~$1.5m in August 2026) is deductible from the state base. The 2025 federal budget act caps the deductibility of gambling losses at 90% of winnings from tax year 2026, a bettor-level friction that disproportionately affects high-volume players and may shade handle at the margin. For B2Tech, the base case should be 10% of promo-deductible AGEWR, but the investment case must survive (i) loss of the promo deduction and (ii) a 20–45% rate on scale; perversely, the proposed $75m handle threshold would favour a mid-tier entrant that stays below it.

segments.name: Payments, responsible gambling, advertising & enforcement
segments.headline: Standard US rails and player-protection rules, a $500k-minimum segregated reserve, state set-off of winnings, and self-reported data that ADG itself disclaims.
narrative: ADG does not publish deposit-method data, so payments reality is inferred from the rule set and operator practice rather than regulator statistics [n/a]. The ADG event wagering rules (A.A.C. R19-4) require player funds to be held in dedicated accounts used for all deposits, receipts and disbursements, backed by a reserve equal to the greater of $500,000 or the amount owed to player accounts, with a software accounting system that separates and distinguishes all receipts and disbursements; operators file a monthly AGEWR report with system-generated support by the 25th, and ADG's Racing Division permits the retail LEWO locations. Mobile wagering is geofenced to the state. Deposit rails in practice are the national mix — ACH/online banking, debit cards, PayPal and other wallets, prepaid cards and cash at partner venues — and Arizona imposes no state-specific deposit-method prohibitions that we could verify [unverified].

Player protection is administered by ADG's Division of Problem Gambling: minimum age 21, the 1-800-NEXT-STEP helpline, a statewide self-exclusion programme spanning tribal casinos and EWFS, and the 10% of privilege fees retained by ADG partly funding treatment. ADG designated September 2026 Responsible Gaming Education Month with a statewide campaign and asks media to include supportive resources when reporting gambling figures. Arizona also operates a set-off regime under which operators must withhold winnings against past-due obligations — the FY2026 Annual Report tabulates intercepts by agency at $393,600 (Administrative Office of the Courts), $121,973 (child support), $6,353 (SNAP) and $0 (AHCCCS) — and the 2021 fact sheet tied withholding to the federal 1099-MISC reporting threshold. Federally, the 90% cap on gambling-loss deductibility from tax year 2026 is a new player-level friction.

Advertising is governed by ADG rules and licence conditions rather than a statutory code: responsible-gaming messaging and helpline inclusion are required, targeting of under-21s is prohibited, and promotional offers are permitted and (for now) tax-deductible — which is why Arizona remains one of the more promo-intensive US markets (FanDuel's $10.5m January 2026 outlay; market-wide 2.3–3.3% of handle). No cap on bonus value, affiliate marketing or college-sports advertising exists at state level [unverified for any pending 2026 rulemaking].

On enforcement and data integrity, two points matter. First, since May 2025 every ADG monthly report carries a disclaimer that figures are operator self-reported, unaudited and subject to adjustment; the FY2026 Annual Report notes ADG received 13 of 14 independent FY2025 audit reports under §5-1319 and is still reconciling over- and under-payments, so monthly series can be restated. Second, the regulatory perimeter is being tested by federally regulated prediction markets (Kalshi and peers) — Utah sued Kalshi in the week of this report — but no Arizona-specific enforcement action against prediction markets was verified in this research [n/a]. For B2Tech, compliance set-up costs are conventional (reserve, segregated accounts, monthly reporting, annual audit, set-off integration) and the RG regime is light-touch by UK standards; the material risk sits in the tax politics, not the conduct rules.

highlights.text: Fiscal regime is among the most operator-friendly in the US: 10% mobile / 8% retail on AGEWR with the 0.25% federal excise and free-bet/promo credits deductible — an effective ~6–7% of gross win and ~0.6% of handle in August 2026, versus NY 51%, IL 20–40% plus per-bet fees, NJ 19.75%.
Deep, mobile-native demand: FY2026 handle $9.08bn, CY2025 GGR $838.7m (+18.5%), 99.7% mobile; #5 US state by handle in August 2025. Even the 2026 trough month ($582.8m) is 17% above August 2024.

Licence supply has re-opened: ADG began accepting applications for available operator licences in May 2026 and allocated one to Circa Sports (San Juan Southern Paiute designee) on 3 Aug 2026 — proof that a tribe-designee route to a fresh allocation is executable, with two to three further slots apparently vacant.

Promo intensity is easing — ~$13m (2.3% of handle, ~27% of pre-promo AGEWR) in August 2026 versus $18.4m (3.0%, 31%) a year earlier — which lowers the cost of defending share for incumbents and the cost of acquisition benchmarks for an entrant.

Fantasy pick'em is a legal, lightly taxed (5% of adjusted revenue) adjacency worth $144m of FY2026 entry fees and $26.6m of adjusted revenue, led by PrizePicks (43%) — a cross-sell channel few European operators exploit.

The proposed 45% tier is keyed to ≥$75m monthly handle, so a mid-tier entrant at $30–55m would be exempt — an asymmetric fiscal position relative to the four scale operators if any version of the tier is ever enacted.

lowlights.text: Tax-rate escalation is a live political project: Governor Hobbs' FY2027 budget proposed 45% on operators with ≥$75m monthly handle ($145.9m FY27 → $202.4m FY29). It was not enacted, but the 'record handle, falling tax' narrative (June 2026: handle +22%, fees −39%) makes a 2027 reprise — possibly as promo-deduction repeal or a per-bet fee — probable.

Statutory sunset of the promo deduction after year five (from 15 Apr 2021) would raise the taxable base ~30–40% at constant GGR; ADG's operative timing is unverified, and deductions were still being taken in June and August 2026.

Concentration leaves little room: FanDuel + DraftKings 60% of August handle, top four 82%, no operator outside the top six above 2%. Sporttrade exited after $20.4m cumulative handle; ESPN Bet was folded into theScore Bet. A licence is access, not share.

Access is gated by the 20-licence cap (10 tribal / 10 pro-sports) and requires a designee agreement with a tribe or franchise on private revenue-share terms; the most recent allocation went to a tribe-backed entrant, and remaining vacancies are few.

Growth has decelerated sharply: August −4.6% YoY and May −4.3%, a two-year August CAGR of +8.3% versus +23% YoY in 2025; the June–July 2026 spikes look event-driven (World Cup) rather than structural.

Reported data is self-reported and unaudited (ADG disclaimer since May 2025; 13 of 14 FY2025 audits received, reconciliations ongoing) — market-share and hold series can be restated, and August 2026 revenue lines in this brief are derived from payouts and fees rather than read from audited line items.
No iGaming optionality: casino gaming is tribal-exclusive under the 2021 compact and no online casino bill moved in 2026; the regulated pool is sports plus fantasy only.

forecast.intro: The rule set in force for August 2026 is unchanged from launch — 10% mobile / 8% retail on promo-deductible AGEWR, 5% on fantasy, a 20-licence cap — but three variables are moving. First, the governor's 45% tier for ≥$75m-handle operators was floated for FY2027 and not enacted; the fiscal gap it was meant to fill (~$950m of uncertain revenue) has not gone away and the legislature's composition after the November 2026 election will determine whether a recalibrated version (lower rate, promo-deduction repeal, or an Illinois-style per-bet fee) appears in the January 2027 executive budget. Second, the statutory five-year promo-deduction sunset is, on a literal reading, already past; how and when ADG applies it is the largest single swing factor for the taxable base. Third, licence supply: ADG re-opened applications in May 2026 and allocated a slot to Circa in August, with launch expected in Q1 2027; two to three further allocations are plausible over 12–18 months. Overlaying all three is the data-integrity cycle — ADG is still reconciling FY2025 audits — and the federal prediction-market question, on which Arizona has not yet shown its hand.

forecast.view: Our independent view: FY2027 handle of **$9.3–9.8bn (+3–8%)** [estimate], with September–November 2026 the swing months (October 2025 set the $967.1m record) and the Super Bowl/March Madness window the ceiling; gross hold settling at **8.5–9.5%** as parlay mix offsets normalising sports outcomes, giving **GGR of ~$850–920m** [estimate]. Promo deductions drift down toward 2% of handle as the big two defend margin rather than share, so taxable AGEWR grows faster than GGR even without the statutory sunset; with the sunset applied, the state's take could approach **$75–85m** at the current 10% rate [estimate]. On rates, we put the probability of a materially higher regime (promo-deduction repeal and/or a tiered rate of 20%+ on scale operators) being enacted for FY2028 at **roughly one in three** — higher than for most Republican-led legislatures because the 'fee' framing offers a route around Prop 108 and because Illinois has normalised tiered structures. Market structure stays a duopoly-plus: FanDuel and DraftKings at 58–62% of handle, Fanatics consolidating #3 at 11–13%, and churn continuing below 2% share; Circa is the one entrant with a differentiated model and its 2027 traction is the test case for any B2Tech entry. Leverage for the state is rising, for operators falling: an entrant should underwrite Arizona at **10% headline, 20% stress and 45% tail for any book above $75m monthly handle**, with no promo deduction in the base case from FY2028.
watch: ADG September–November 2026 reports (mid-November onward): whether the NFL season restores YoY growth against the record Oct-25 ($967.1m) and Nov-25 ($965.2m) comps, and whether promo deductions fall below 2% of handle.

Governor Hobbs' FY2028 executive budget (January 2027) and the post-election legislature: any reprise of the 45% tier, a promo-deduction repeal, or a per-bet fee; watch for the 'fee vs tax' Prop 108 argument being tested.
ADG's written position on the five-year promo-deduction sunset under §5-1301(1) — any bulletin, rule change or reporting-form revision that removes the deduction line.
Circa Sports Arizona launch (targeted Q1 2027) and any further licence allocations from the May 2026 application window; terms of tribe-designee deals as a benchmark for B2Tech partner negotiations.
ADG audit outcomes under §5-1319 (14th FY2025 audit, over/under-payment reconciliations) and any restatement of monthly handle/revenue series.

Arizona's posture on federally regulated prediction markets (Kalshi, Robinhood et al.) following Utah's lawsuit — a cease-and-desist or litigation would signal perimeter enforcement; silence signals leakage from the taxed base.
Fantasy pick'em regulation: any ADG move to reclassify against-the-house pick'em as event wagering (10% vs 5%).
